step_title: Clear pending dues on the vehicle
step_description: Check and pay off any pending e-challans, road tax, or hypothecation before initiating transfer; the Vahan portal commonly blocks a transfer application if unpaid traffic-camera fines exist on the vehicle.
action_required: Pay pending challans/taxes; obtain financier NOC (Form 35) if the vehicle was financed
failure_consequence: Transfer application blocked until dues are cleared

step_title: Seller logs in and validates vehicle details
step_description: Seller logs into the Vahan portal (or visits the RTO), enters the vehicle registration number and the last five digits of the chassis number to validate/fetch the RC record, and verifies identity via mobile OTP.
action_required: Log in and validate vehicle/chassis details
failure_consequence: Cannot proceed to Form 29 without successful validation

step_description: Seller navigates to RC Related Services > Transfer of Ownership > Notice of Transfer, and fills Form 29 with the buyers details and the date of sale.
deadline_from_event: commonly cited as within 14 days (intra-state) or 45 days (interstate) of the sale (NOT_VERIFIED against a primary gazette source)
failure_consequence: Continuing legal liability for the seller (e.g. for challans or an offence committed by the buyer) as the registered owner of record until transfer is completed

step_description: Buyer receives the acknowledgment/reference from the sellers Form 29 filing and completes Form 30 with their own identity and address details.
failure_consequence: RC remains in the sellers name until Form 30 is completed

step_title: Upload supporting documents and pay transfer fee
step_description: Both parties upload scanned/digitally signed copies of Form 29 and 30, ID and address proof, insurance, and (if applicable) the financier NOC; the applicable transfer fee is paid online.
action_required: Upload documents and complete fee payment
completion_evidence: Payment confirmation and document upload receipt
failure_consequence: Application remains incomplete/pending until all documents and fees are submitted

step_title: RTO verification (and physical appearance where required)
step_description: The application is reviewed by the Registering Authority; in States without a fully faceless process, the buyer and/or seller may need to visit the RTO in person for document verification.
action_required: Verify submitted documents; conduct physical verification where the State does not offer a fully online/faceless process
deadline_from_event: commonly cited as 7-30 days for processing (NOT_VERIFIED, varies by State)
failure_consequence: Application may be rejected or sent back for correction if documents are inconsistent

step_title: New RC issued in buyers name
step_description: Once approved, a new Registration Certificate reflecting the buyer as the registered owner is generated and dispatched; the registration number itself remains unchanged.
action_required: Issue and dispatch the updated RC
deadline_from_event: commonly cited as an additional 3-6 weeks for physical smart-card delivery (NOT_VERIFIED)
completion_evidence: Updated RC (physical smart card and/or digital copy via DigiLocker/mParivahan)
failure_consequence: Buyer cannot be treated as the legal owner for insurance, resale, or liability purposes until this step is completed

step_description: Claimant collects the FIR/police accident report, medical treatment records or post-mortem report, and evidence of the deceased/injured persons income and dependants.
action_required: Compile FIR, medical/post-mortem records, income proof
failure_consequence: Claim petition may be returned or delayed for want of supporting evidence

step_title: Choose between Section 166 and Section 163A route
step_description: Claimant (with legal counsel) decides whether to pursue a full fault-based claim under Section 166, or the faster structured-formula claim under Section 163A; per Deepal Girishbhai Soni v. United India Insurance Co., these are mutually exclusive alternatives.
completion_evidence: Claim petition indicating the chosen route
failure_consequence: Choosing the wrong route, or attempting to claim under both, can result in the petition being rejected or restricted to the structured-formula amount

step_title: Draft and file the claim petition
step_description: Claimant files the compensation claim petition before the MACT having jurisdiction over the accident location, claimants residence, or defendants residence.
deadline_from_event: no fixed statutory limitation period under the MV Act; Tribunals commonly entertain delayed claims with sufficient cause (NOT_VERIFIED as an absolute rule)
failure_consequence: Delay may require explanation to the Tribunal, though it is not an absolute bar to relief

step_description: Insurer and/or vehicle owner are given notice and an opportunity to contest; the Tribunal examines evidence on a preponderance-of-probability standard (per Bimla Devi v. HRTC), not the stricter criminal standard.
failure_consequence: Case may proceed ex parte if the opposing party does not appear despite notice

step_description: Tribunal computes just compensation applying the Sarla Verma multiplier framework and the Pranay Sethi standardised heads (future prospects, conventional amounts for loss of consortium/estate/funeral expenses).
failure_consequence: Dissatisfied party may appeal to the jurisdictional High Court

step_description: Applicant registers on the Sarathi portal and fills Form 2, selecting the vehicle class(es) for which the Learners Licence is sought.
failure_consequence: Cannot proceed without a complete Form 2

step_description: Applicant uploads scanned age proof and address proof documents as required for the selected vehicle class.
failure_consequence: Application rejected without valid age/address proof

step_description: Applicant pays the LL application fee online per the CMVR Rule 32 fee schedule.
failure_consequence: Application remains pending until fee is paid

step_title: Take the online Learners Licence test
step_description: Applicant appears for the mandatory online multiple-choice test on traffic rules and signs, either at home or at an RTO kiosk depending on State practice.
failure_consequence: Repeat attempt required if the test is failed, subject to a State-specific cooling period (NOT_VERIFIED)

step_description: On passing the test, the Learners Licence is generated, valid for 6 months, during which the applicant may practice driving under the supervision of a licensed driver.
failure_consequence: Applicant cannot legally drive unsupervised, or apply for a Permanent DL, without this issued LL

step_description: Applicant confirms their Learners Licence has been held for at least 30 days and has not expired (LL valid for 6 months from issue).
deadline_from_event: 30 days minimum from LL issue; before 6-month LL expiry
failure_consequence: Application rejected outside the eligible window; may require a fresh LL if the window has lapsed

step_description: Applicant books an available driving test slot at the RTO (or a Government-accredited driving training school) online.
failure_consequence: Cannot proceed to the driving test without a booked slot

step_title: Appear for and pass the driving test
step_description: Applicant appears at the RTO test track for the practical driving skill test appropriate to the vehicle class applied for.
failure_consequence: If failed, applicant must rebook and reattempt, subject to a State-specific cooling period (NOT_VERIFIED)

step_description: On passing the test, applicants photograph, signature, and biometric details are captured at the RTO (where required), and the applicable fee is paid.
action_required: Complete biometric capture and fee payment
failure_consequence: Licence cannot be printed/issued without this step

step_description: The Permanent Driving Licence is generated and dispatched to the applicant (smart card by post, and/or made available digitally via DigiLocker/mParivahan).
failure_consequence: Applicant should carry the LL or a valid interim acknowledgment until the DL is received

step_description: Dealer issues Form 21 (Sale Certificate) to the buyer at the time of purchase, along with the vehicle invoice.
failure_consequence: Registration application cannot proceed without proof of sale

step_description: If the vehicle needs to be driven before permanent registration is complete (e.g. taken from dealer to home State), a Temporary Registration Certificate is obtained.
deadline_from_event: before driving the vehicle in a public place without permanent RC
failure_consequence: Vehicle should not be driven in a public place without either temporary or permanent registration

step_title: File Form 20 application for permanent registration
step_description: Owner (typically via the dealer) files Form 20, the primary registration application, along with insurance and PUC (where applicable).
deadline_from_event: commonly cited as within 7 days of taking delivery for permanent registration (NOT_VERIFIED exact statutory day-count)
failure_consequence: Vehicle cannot be legally used in a public place without valid registration

step_title: Pay road tax and registration fee
step_description: Owner pays the applicable one-time road tax (State-specific) and CMVR registration fee.
action_required: Complete road tax and fee payment
failure_consequence: Registration cannot be completed without payment

step_title: Permanent RC issued and number plate assigned
step_description: Registering Authority approves the application, assigns a permanent registration number, and issues the Registration Certificate (Form 23).
completion_evidence: Issued RC (Form 23) and assigned registration number
failure_consequence: Vehicle cannot legally continue in use in a public place beyond the temporary registration period without this step

step_title: Report the accident to the nearest police station
step_description: Driver, victim, or witness reports the accident to the police station having jurisdiction over the accident location, providing details of the vehicles, parties, and circumstances involved.
online_portal: State e-FIR portal (where available for applicable accident types)
deadline_from_event: promptly; a drivers own statutory duty to report is time-bound (exact hours NOT_VERIFIED)
failure_consequence: Failure to report promptly by a driver involved may itself constitute a separate offence (see legal_provisions: accident-reporting duty, PROV_MVA_S132_PENDING_ADD)

step_description: Police record statements, document the accident scene, and (where death or serious injury is involved) coordinate medical/post-mortem examination.
failure_consequence: Absence of thorough documentation can weaken a subsequent MACT claim, though it is not by itself fatal to the claim (per Bimla Devi v. HRTC on the standard of proof)

step_title: Obtain FIR copy for insurance/compensation use
step_description: Complainant obtains a certified copy of the FIR, used as supporting evidence for insurance claims and any subsequent MACT compensation petition.
failure_consequence: Insurance claim or MACT petition may face additional scrutiny without a police report, though case law does not treat it as an absolute bar
